title: Fox
intro: Fox repeatedly gives ordinary discomfort an inflated public costume: a shaving nick becomes an imperial medical crisis, urban pettiness becomes international, and a private desire becomes top secret. Those enlargements promise importance without producing security. The speaker's confident future keeps meeting bad directions, tight circumstances and weary sighs. At the end, a whole corrupted city contracts into one remembered classroom humiliation. The sound-chain carries the scene onward, while the memory suggests how small bodily incidents can outlast grand claims to have moved on.
reading: Inflated authority fails at mundane care; apparent adulthood and worldly confidence are interrupted by school humiliation.

revisions.26-n1: The tiny shaving injury escalates through prestigious treatment into death, then the physicians are called performers and quacks. The joke starts with disproportion but lands on failed competence: the impressive apparatus makes the ordinary problem worse. That pattern recurs when international grandeur produces small-mindedness. The lyric repeatedly tests a large title against what happens to the person relying on it.
revisions.editorial-26-classified: What must be protected is simply what he wants. Calling it top secret makes private desire sound like a state-level asset, but the following scheming and deceptive appearances give the precaution an emotional logic. Knowing the wish would give other people a way to manipulate it. This is the guarded counterpart to 'Bakery Session', where another person notices and reassures his desire instead of exploiting it.
revisions.26-phrase-emperor: The emperor's nonexistent clothing is exposed by a child, which makes the instruction to retain a childlike heart more pointed. It follows images of a human exterior concealing an animal interior and an animal skin worn as a coat. Clothing keeps failing as evidence of what someone is. The child offers plain sight in a world of elaborate presentation, though the final school memory complicates any idea of childhood as uncomplicated safety.
revisions.26-n4: The teacher's phlegm interrupts the scale of Gotham's corruption with a memory too specific and disgusting to become a heroic origin story. The rhymes then carry phlegm into guts, bad grades and an egg mouldering under bedding. Sound is visibly organising the sequence; not every object needs a separate symbolic key. What holds the passage emotionally is the reduction from public menace to a frightened, ashamed body that has not forgotten the classroom.
